name: Shell Game
description: A term shifts meaning slightly between the stimulus and the answer choice, or between premise and conclusion.
whyTempting: The words look the same on a skim.
tell: Check whether the term means exactly the same thing in both places.

name: Too Strong
description: An answer overstates what the stimulus's evidence actually supports (uses 'always'/'never'/'guarantees' where the stimulus only supports 'sometimes'/'tends to').
whyTempting: It's directionally correct, just overstated.
tell: Check the strength words against the strength of the original claim.

name: Reversed Conditional
description: Mistakes p→q for q→p (the mistaken reversal).
whyTempting: Feels like a natural paraphrase if you're not tracking direction.
tell: Re-derive the contrapositive and check the direction explicitly.

name: New Information in Must-Be-True
description: An inference answer introduces a claim not actually supported by anything in the stimulus.
whyTempting: Sounds plausible and topically related.
tell: Ask: can I point to the specific sentence(s) that force this to be true?

name: True But Irrelevant
description: A factually plausible statement that doesn't actually bear on the argument's logic.
whyTempting: It sounds like real-world common sense.
tell: Ask whether the answer, if true or false, would actually change the argument's strength.

name: Opposite Task
description: An answer that does the opposite of what the stem asked (weakens instead of strengthens, etc.).
whyTempting: Usually from misreading the stem, especially on EXCEPT questions.
tell: Reread the stem before reading the answer choices, every time.

name: Half-Right Flaw Description
description: A flaw description that's correct about part of the argument but mischaracterizes the actual logical gap.
whyTempting: Uses real vocabulary from the stimulus.
tell: Match the flaw description to the specific gap, not just to the topic.

name: Premise Restatement
description: A Main Point trap: restates a supporting premise as if it were the conclusion.
whyTempting: It's a true, on-topic statement from the stimulus.
tell: Apply the 'therefore' test — does this read naturally as the payoff of everything else?

name: Scope Shift
description: An answer subtly broadens or narrows the scope (a subgroup becomes the whole group, or vice versa).
whyTempting: Close enough on a fast read.
tell: Check quantifiers and group boundaries word for word.

name: Comparative Not Supported
description: An answer makes a comparison ('more than', 'better than') the stimulus never actually establishes.
whyTempting: Comparisons feel like natural inferences.
tell: Check whether both sides of the comparison were actually measured/discussed.

name: Wrong Viewpoint Attribution
description: A true, correctly-worded claim from the passage attributed to the wrong person (critic's view stated as the author's, or vice versa).
whyTempting: The words genuinely appear in the passage.
tell: Check the viewpoint inventory before trusting a content match.

name: Extreme Overstatement
description: An RC answer overstates what the passage actually claims.
whyTempting: It's in the right direction, just too strong.
tell: Compare strength words in the answer to strength words in the passage.

name: Out of Scope
description: An answer introduces a topic or claim the passage never actually discusses.
whyTempting: Sounds topically related and plausible.
tell: Ask: which sentence in the passage actually supports this?

name: Half Right, Half Wrong
description: An answer with one correct clause and one incorrect or unsupported clause.
whyTempting: The correct half anchors your attention.
tell: Verify every clause of the answer independently, not just the first half.

name: True But Not What Was Asked
description: A factually accurate passage statement that doesn't answer the specific question being asked.
whyTempting: It's verifiably true, which feels like enough.
tell: Reread the stem's exact task before checking factual accuracy.

name: Too Narrow Main Point
description: A Main Point answer that only captures one paragraph's content rather than the whole passage's point.
whyTempting: It's accurate as far as it goes.
tell: Check the answer against every paragraph, not just the one that comes to mind first.

name: Word Match Trap
description: An answer reuses distinctive vocabulary from the passage without actually matching its meaning or claim.
whyTempting: Familiar words create false confidence.
tell: Check meaning, not vocabulary overlap.

name: Comparative: Only One Passage Addressed
description: On comparative-passage questions, an answer that's true of only one of the two passages when the question asks about both.
whyTempting: It's accurate about the passage you remember best.
tell: Explicitly check both passages before confirming a comparative answer.

name: EXCEPT Stem Flip
description: Misreading an EXCEPT stem and solving for the normal task instead of its inverse.
whyTempting: EXCEPT is easy to skim past under time pressure.
tell: Read every EXCEPT stem twice before touching the answer choices.

name: Misread the Task
description: Confusing two similar-sounding stems (e.g. Necessary vs Sufficient Assumption) and solving for the wrong standard.
whyTempting: The stems share vocabulary.
tell: Identify the exact family and standard before reading answer choices.
